# 10 One answer for a repeated `timeline:` header

## Outcome

All three diagram kinds treat a second `timeline:` inside an open timeline block the same way: an
error. `parseFlowchart` stops re-checking the header once it is in timeline mode, and consequently
calls `parseTimelineBody` like the other two — so no parser retains a drain loop of its own, which
is what ticket 08 was supposed to achieve and could not.

## Why this ticket exists

Ticket 08 discovered, and deliberately preserved, a divergence nobody had chosen. Measured, not
inferred:

```
flowchart:  document parsed, entries kept, diagnostics []
class:      document null, error: Unrecognized timeline line: "timeline:"
sequence:   document null, error: Unrecognized timeline line: "timeline:"
```

The cause is ordering, not intent. `parseFlowchart.ts:88` tests `isTimelineHeader(line)`
unconditionally, before the `mode === "timeline"` branch at `:141` can see the line — so a repeated
header re-enters timeline mode and is swallowed. The other two parsers hand the line to the grammar,
which reports it.

The repo owner chose to unify on the error. It is the answer consistent with the rule all three
parsers already share — an unrecognized line inside a block is a diagnostic — and flowchart was
only escaping it by accident of loop order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A flowchart document with a second `timeline:` inside its timeline block reports
      `Unrecognized timeline line: "timeline:"` and returns a null document, matching class and
      sequence exactly — same message, same severity, and a line/column pointing at the repeat.
- [x] Assert all three kinds produce the identical diagnostic for the identical construct, in one
      test, so a future divergence fails rather than being discovered by an extraction three boards
      later.
- [x] `parseFlowchart` calls `parseTimelineBody`, not `parseTimelineBodyLine`. No parser retains a
      per-line drain loop. Delete the comment at `:141-147` explaining the divergence — it will be
      describing something that no longer exists.
- [~] `parseTimelineBodyLine` is NOT un-exported: the condition is false. It still has an importer
      outside its module -- `parseTimelineBlock.test.ts` exercises it in two cases. The worker
      checked rather than assumed, which is what this criterion asked for, and the answer was no.
      Follow-up: fold those two cases into `parseTimelineBody` tests (both are observable through
      the drain), then un-export. Originally: un-export if this leaves it with no caller outside
      `parseTimelineBlock.ts`. Check rather than assume; `parseTimelineLine` was un-exported for
      the same reason in `907fc24`.
- [x] Every other existing flowchart timeline test passes **unedited**. The only behavior that may
      change is the repeated-header case.
- [x] The `examples/` enumeration test (added in `3589544`) still passes — it renders all eight
      documents, so it is the safety net for this being a behavior change. If an example breaks,
      stop and report it rather than editing the example.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s **Timeline block** entry states that the block is declared once and a second
      `timeline:` inside it is an error, in all three kinds. This is the decision's durable record.

## Test seam

`parseSiren` through the source string, for all three kinds. There is no `parseFlowchart.test.ts`;
flowchart parser tests live in `parseSiren.test.ts`.
